AZUSA CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
AGENDA
June 23, 2021
07:00 P.M.
NOTICE: A copy of the following public hearing staff reports and Initial Studies, if applicable, for the Planning Commission projects will be available for review during regular working hours of 7:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Monday - Thursday at the Planning Division and during regular hours of the Azusa City Library. Any questions regarding any agenda item may be answered by the Planning Division at (626) 812-5017. The Planning Commission Meetings are held at 7:00 p.m. in the Azusa Civic Auditorium at 213 East Foothill Boulevard, Azusa, California.
CORONAVIRUS (COVID-19) ADVISORY
Due to the state and local State of Emergency resulting from the threat of Novel Coronavirus (COVID-19), Governor Newsom has issued Executive Order N-29-20 in which Section 3 supersedes Paragraph 11 of Executive Order N-25-20 (issued on March 12, 2020) addressing Brown Act regulations. This new order states that the City does not need to make a physical location available for members of the public to observe a public meeting and offer public comment. The Order allows the City to hold City Council/Board meetings via teleconferencing and allows for members of the public to observe and address the meeting telephonically or electronically.
To follow the new Order issued by the Governor, the Planning Commission meeting scheduled for Wednesday, December 9, 2020 at 7:00 p.m. will be closed to the public. Members of the public may submit Public Comments by 6:30 p.m. electronically only by emailing PublicComment@azusaca.gov. Emailed public comments will be sent to all Planning Commission Members and will be part of the record. (Comments shall be limited to no more than 250 words). View the Planning Commission meeting live at the City's website https://www.ci.azusa.ca.us/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or Channel 3 (Spectrum).

1.
Case No.: V-2019-03 Location: 1054 E. Alford Street, Azusa, CA
APN: 8629-007-024
Applicant: Leo Angelo Madarang
The City of Azusa received a request to allow for a reduction in the rear-yard setback from the required 25 feet to 10 feet. The Variance has been requested after the fact. The previously approved breezeway connecting the dwelling to the detached accessory structure (garage) has been converted into habitable space without building permits.
The California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”) exempts projects that a public agency rejects or disapproves. (Cal. Pub. Resources Code, § 21080 (b)(5) [CEQA “does not apply to apply to…[p]rojects which a public agency rejects or disapproves”]; see also State CEQA Guidelines, § 15061 (b)(4).) Accordingly, the Planning Commission’s denial of the Variance is exempt from CEQA.

2.
Case No.: DR-2021-12, UP-2021-02 Location: 100 N. Old San Gabriel Canyon Rd., Azusa, California
APN: 8684-027-901, 902, & -903
Applicant: Johnathan Perisho (Watershed Conservation Authority)
The City of Azusa received a request to approve Phase I of the Watershed Conservation Authority's River Wilderness Park Master Plan which will include site improvements such as a new restroom structure, detached pavilion, loop trail, rest stop, river overlooks, adventure play area, entry gateway, extending bike trail along SR-39, water and sewer lines, undergrounding of electrical, grading, landscaping, and reconfiguration of the parking lot. Additionally, a Use Permit for conference facility.
This project has already prepared two Initial Study - Mitigated Negative Declarations (IS-MNDs) and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Plans for the entire Wilderness Park Master Plan.
